reason: No cited evidence is provided to support any of the key premises. The claims about Si-induced liquid-phase sintering, grain-boundary segregation, preferential oxidation to a continuous SiO2 scale, and the resulting protection against oxidation and liquid-metal corrosion are all specific and require prior experimental or theoretical backing, which is absent.
premises: Si addition induces transient liquid phase that enables densification at ~1650°C
Si segregates to grain boundaries in sintered ZrB2
Grain-boundary Si preferentially oxidizes to form a continuous protective SiO2 scale
SiO2 scale enhances oxidation resistance and liquid-metal corrosion resistance
Microalloyed Si does not form excessive secondary glassy phase that degrades mechanical properties
